findings.title: The write step's re-read is not inside a transaction unless it starts with BEGIN IMMEDIATE
findings.why_it_matters: D2's safety argument is that the fresh re-read and the watermark stamp are atomic with the vector writes, but the design never says how the transaction opens. Both ways of building it from the text as written fail. Under Python's default mode the re-read runs in autocommit, another writer can commit before the first DML, and the stamp is decided from stale data, which is the false watermark the design exists to prevent. With an explicit deferred `BEGIN`, a commit landing after the re-read makes the first write fail instantly with `database is locked`, because `busy_timeout` doesn't apply to that upgrade, and that loss lands right after the expensive inference.
findings.chosen: Add to D2's pinned list: "The write step runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before the re-read, then re-reads, checks, writes, prunes, stamps, and commits, so `busy_timeout` waits for the lock and nothing can commit between the check and the stamp. A test interleaves a competing commit between the read and the first write." This doesn't need extending to D3's clear or D4's sentinel as operational-resilience proposed: each is a single-statement write with no earlier read to upgrade from, and the probe shows that form succeeds and takes the normal busy wait. If Finding 6 makes the sentinel conditional on a re-read, it needs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` too.

findings.title: A branch that stays eligible is re-selected at the head of every later batch, then aborts the run
findings.why_it_matters: The Posture and D4 say a lost write "costs one item" and "the run continues", but neither says how the failed branch is left out. Selection is `ORDER BY id LIMIT 20` with no exclusion, so with per-branch commits the unfinished branch is the lowest eligible id and sits first in every later batch. It gets inferred again each time, which is a retry loop despite the "no retries" stance. When it's the only branch left, the batch repeats, `run_batch_loop` calls `on_stuck`, and the run ends with `EXIT_ABORT`. The 20-branch batch no longer maps to a commit boundary, but the stuck guard still assumes it does.
findings.recommended: A: Forward-only pass: `select_batch_cb` adds `AND id > ?` using the last id seen, so a run never revisits a branch
findings.chosen: A: Forward-only pass: `select_batch_cb` adds `AND id > ?` using the last id seen, so a run never revisits a branch

findings.title: "Current chunk" is undefined, and the existing predicate can't prove a vector exists
findings.why_it_matters: D2 says a vector doesn't replace a chunk "already current at equal or better quality", and stamps by `_should_stamp_watermark`'s conditions, but that predicate checks only version, hash, and cap, not model or `chunk_vec` presence. D5 removes the pre-delete that today handles version-stale, wrong-model, and vector-less chunks, so D2's skip rule now has to recognize them. Read as "hash and cap match", the skip would refuse the replacement D5 selected: the branch stays eligible and re-infers without ever healing, which then feeds Finding 2. The next `EMBEDDING_VERSION` bump is the case that hits this, because every chunk is then version-stale with a matching hash.
findings.chosen: Add to D2: "A chunk is current when its `content_hash` matches, its `embedding_version` and `embedding_model` are current, and a `chunk_vec` row exists. D2's write-skip additionally requires `effective_cap_tokens` at least that of the vector being written; the stamp requires `MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Backfill's diff (D5) selects the same chunks this excludes. Sync's diff stays narrower per H6." Update D2's lock-time row from about 4 ms to about 10 ms to include the vector-presence check.

findings.title: Skip, discard, and withheld-stamp outcomes have no specified log line
findings.why_it_matters: The design adds outcomes that run unattended and leave a branch unembedded: sync skipping inference for a live backfill (D7), a vector discarded on hash mismatch (D2), and a stamp withheld because the proof failed. The Posture only requires logging a failed embed and a write timeout. Without lines for the rest, you can't tell whether Finding 2 is happening, how often D7 delays vectors, or why a branch remains unembedded. These are dark operations under `logging.md`, which requires a signal from unattended processes.
findings.chosen: Add to the Posture's Failure handling line: "Each outcome that leaves a branch unembedded logs a line with the branch id: sync's backfill skip at INFO with the marker PID, and the write step's discarded-on-hash count and withheld stamp at INFO. The backfill's existing completion line adds the count of branches attempted and not updated." This is log lines only, and the "no new metrics" stance stands.

findings.title: D7 infers backfill liveness from a PID marker, so a reused PID silences sync inference
findings.why_it_matters: D7 decides "a backfill is inferring" from `os.kill(pid, 0)` on a marker, which proves only that some process has that PID. A SIGKILLed or OOM-killed backfill leaves its marker behind because the CLI's `finally` never runs. If that PID is later reused, sync skips inference for as long as the other process lives, and the same marker already blocks the next backfill, so new sessions get no vectors. Keyword search and stored messages are unaffected, and vectors catch up once the marker clears.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a stale backfill marker whose PID gets reused makes sync skip inference until that process exits or the marker is removed
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a stale backfill marker whose PID gets reused makes sync skip inference until that process exits or the marker is removed

findings.title: The content-error sentinel is decided from a snapshot that may be stale
findings.why_it_matters: D4 writes the `-1` sentinel after `_model_still_healthy`. With inference outside any transaction, the content that failed may have changed by then, so the sentinel lands on a branch whose current content was never tried. Selection excludes `-1`, and a tool-content repair doesn't reset it, so the branch stays out of backfill until a later sync clears it or a link change does.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a branch whose content changes during a failing inference can carry the sentinel until a later sync or link change resets it
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a branch whose content changes during a failing inference can carry the sentinel until a later sync or link change resets it

findings.title: Backfill has no check for a sync already inferring, so peaks can briefly stack
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: 15 GB machines running manual backfill during active use. D7 checks only at the start of sync's inference, so a backfill starting during a sync's inference can overlap it, up to about 12.4 GB of inference at worst. The critic's "kills the box" is stronger than the arithmetic: 12.4 GB fits in 15 GB unless other load is high, and it needs both processes on near-cap text at once. D7's ratification already accepts this overlap by name.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a backfill starting during a sync's inference can briefly stack both memory peaks
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a backfill starting during a sync's inference can briefly stack both memory peaks

findings.title: An inference that exceeds memory kills the run with nothing naming the branch
findings.why_it_matters: An OOM kill bypasses the sentinel path, which only handles Python exceptions, and leaves no record of which branch was running. Since selection is by id, a repeat kill would stop each run at the same point. The change itself improves this, because every earlier branch is now committed, and the critic asks for no design change.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: an OOM kill during backfill doesn't record which branch was running
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: an OOM kill during backfill doesn't record which branch was running

findings.title: Lock-hold claim "Milliseconds" is only measured for the re-read
Findings converge on the no-inference path through the write step
findings.why_it_matters: All three critics landed on one mechanism: `embed_branch_chunks` sending a call with nothing to infer into `_write_step`. From one angle it costs a second write-lock acquisition on every Stop (Finding 2). From another it logs "embedding watermark withheld" on every Stop for a branch holding a draft chunk (Finding 3). It also makes a no-op Stop capable of logging "embedding skipped: database locked". Both local fixes would be unnecessary if a call that would change nothing never reached the write step. The question for you: does this point at the mechanism itself, or are these two small costs of a shape you already ratified, to be handled or accepted one at a time?
findings.recommended: B: Keep the no-inference path through the write step and address Findings 2 and 3 individually.
findings.chosen: B: Keep the no-inference path through the write step and address Findings 2 and 3 individually.

findings.title: Every Stop now takes a second write lock and rewrites the stamp, even with nothing to embed
findings.why_it_matters: The no-work path runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, re-reads and re-hashes the whole branch, reads chunks twice, and runs the stamp `UPDATE` even when the value is already current. The lock acquisition is a new failure point: a Stop whose messages committed can log "embedding skipped: database locked; left for backfill" about a no-op, after waiting up to 30 s behind an import.
findings.recommended: A: Return without taking the lock when nothing needs writing, pruning, or stamping.
findings.chosen: A: Return without taking the lock when nothing needs writing, pruning, or stamping.
findings.choice_reason: Asked why not A; the stated cost was overstated, and the recommendation changed to A after correction.

findings.title: "embedding watermark withheld" logs at INFO on every Stop for a branch with a draft chunk
findings.why_it_matters: Sync's diff deliberately leaves draft and version-stale chunks alone, so `_should_stamp_watermark` keeps returning False and `_apply_write` logs the line on every Stop. Nothing has changed since the previous line. The Posture asks for a line when an outcome leaves a branch unembedded, not a repeat on each unchanged state. A user who never runs the opt-in backfill gets this for the life of the session. It also speeds rotation of a 1 MB log and buries the lines that matter.
findings.chosen: In `_apply_write`, log the withheld line at INFO only when inference ran this call (`prepared` is non-empty), and at DEBUG otherwise. This keeps the Posture's line for a stamp withheld after a real embed. Don't add the reason field senior-engineer suggested: it would change what `_should_stamp_watermark` returns, and only one critic asked for it.

findings.title: D2's "BEGIN IMMEDIATE before the re-read" has no test that fails if the order breaks
findings.why_it_matters: D2 lists this as behavior to pin, and it's why the stamp is true at commit. Moving `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` after the first SELECT passes every current test, because Python's legacy transaction mode doesn't open a transaction on reads. The regression would appear only under real contention, as a false stamp or a `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` that `is_database_locked` reports as an ordinary lock timeout.
findings.chosen: Add a test on a file DB with `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` set for that test. Set a `set_trace_callback` on `conn` that fires when the re-read's `SELECT 1 FROM branches` runs. In the callback, have `other` (busy_timeout 0) attempt `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, record whether it raised a locked `OperationalError`, and roll back `other` if it got the lock. Assert on the recorded result after the embed returns, because sqlite3 swallows exceptions raised inside trace callbacks. This tests the lock itself, so it subsumes senior-engineer's statement-order assertion.

findings.title: A write lost after inference logs the same line as a cheap clear timeout, so D8's revisit condition can't be evaluated
findings.why_it_matters: D8 says to reconsider "if logs after shipping show lost writes essentially never happen", but the logs can't show that. The clear (before inference, costing nothing) and the write step (after inference, costing all of it) raise the same `OperationalError`, and each caller logs them as one case. At 2am you can't tell whether the nightly run lost minutes of inference or nothing.
findings.chosen: Around the final `_write_step` call in `embed_branch_chunks`, catch `sqlite3.OperationalError`. When `is_database_locked` is true, log a WARNING such as "embed write lost to a lock; inference discarded" with `branch_id` and `selected=len(prepared)`, then re-raise so callers behave as today. Import `is_database_locked` beside `commit_single_write` at `src/ccrecall/embed_ops.py:14`. Leave out senior-engineer's `inference_s`, because the Posture rules out new metrics and the selected count shows the cost.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md invariant 3 claims more than the ledger about crashes
findings.why_it_matters: The new text says "A crash at any point leaves the branch selected by backfill". D3 explicitly accepts a window where that's false: sync commits, then crashes before the clear commits, with links unchanged. CLAUDE.md is what future maintainers and agents treat as the contract, so a later change could lean on the stronger sentence.
findings.chosen: Replace that sentence's claim with: "A crash during or after inference leaves the branch selected by backfill; the one unguarded point is between sync's commit and the clear when links didn't change, which the next sync on that session heals." Keep the rest of the sentence ("and those transaction boundaries must not change across module splits").

findings.title: `--limit` now bounds stamped branches, not attempts, so it no longer caps a run
findings.why_it_matters: `total_updated` now counts only stamped branches, and it drives both `limit_reached` and the batch slice. `--limit 5` keeps attempting branches, each a full inference or a 30 s lock wait, until five stamp. Attempted branches still get vectors written, so the run can embed more than N branches. The README says `--limit 500` will "cap this run at 500 branches", and the help text says "at most N". operational-resilience considered this and called it low-value, since each branch is still attempted once and `--limit` is a manual convenience.
findings.recommended: A: Count attempts for `--limit`, using the existing `total_processed`, and keep `updated` for the summary and `remaining`.
findings.chosen: A: Count attempts for `--limit`, using the existing `total_processed`, and keep `updated` for the summary and `remaining`.

findings.title: Nothing measures how long the write step holds the lock
findings.why_it_matters: This change exists to shorten lock holds, but nothing logs how long `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` waited or how long the write step held. A regression where the write step grows would surface only later, as import failures.
findings.recommended: B: Leave it. The import failure count remains the outcome measure.
findings.chosen: B: Leave it. The import failure count remains the outcome measure.

findings.title: Sync's "a backfill is running" is a guess from a PID marker, and a reused PID silently turns off both embed paths
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: a single-user machine with an occasional nightly job; severity rises for a user who runs backfill from a scheduler on a box with PID churn. `live_pid_holder` infers "backfill inference is running" from a marker file plus a signal-0 probe. If backfill dies without cleanup and its PID is reused, sync skips inference. D7 accepted that much. The part D7 doesn't state: the next backfill sees the same live PID and exits 0 "already running", so both paths stay off, with only an INFO line, until that process exits or someone removes the marker. Messages still commit, and vectors catch up afterward, so no data is lost.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation: a stale backfill marker whose PID is reused by a live process keeps both sync inference and backfill off until that process exits or the marker is removed.
findings.chosen: C: Accept as a known limitation: a stale backfill marker whose PID is reused by a live process keeps both sync inference and backfill off until that process exits or the marker is removed.

findings.title: Nothing stops backfill walking the whole backlog at 30 s per branch against a persistent lock holder, and it then exits 0
findings.why_it_matters: Under the ratified posture (from #245) a lock timeout costs one branch and the run continues, and forward-only selection attempts every eligible branch once. With a stuck lock holder, each branch waits out the 30 s clear. The run then returns `EXIT_OK` and calls `clear_embedding_failure()` even if nothing was stamped, so the scheduler and the health sidecar both read it as healthy. Only the completion line's "not updated" count shows it. Previously the abort acted as the brake.
findings.recommended: A: Abort with `EXIT_ABORT` after about 3 consecutive lock timeouts.
findings.chosen: A: Abort with `EXIT_ABORT` after about 3 consecutive lock timeouts.

findings.title: A branch that OOM-kills backfill stays first in line and the log doesn't name it
findings.why_it_matters: Selection is `ORDER BY id`, and an OOM kill bypasses the sentinel path. So if a branch triggers the kill, it remains the lowest eligible id and the next run reaches it again. No line names a branch before inference starts, and progress lines come only every 20 branches. Higher ids aren't reached while the machine can't afford the peak. D4 accepted that an OOM kill doesn't record the branch, but not this follow-on.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation: an OOM kill during backfill doesn't name the branch, and that branch is reached first again next run.
findings.chosen: A: Log one INFO line naming the branch and exchange count before `embed_batch`.

findings.title: "The caller must have no transaction open" is a docstring contract
findings.why_it_matters: A future caller leaving a write open would get one of two results. On the no-work path, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` raises "cannot start a transaction within a transaction", which isn't a lock error, so the nightly run aborts. On the work path, which the critic didn't trace, `commit_single_write` silently commits the caller's open writes along with the clear.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a caller that leaves a write open violates a documented contract, and either aborts the run or commits that write early.
findings.chosen: A: Add the guard at the top of `embed_branch_chunks`, raising `sqlite3.ProgrammingError`.

findings.title: The D3 clear is unconditional, so it can un-stamp a complete branch or erase a content-error sentinel
findings.why_it_matters: The clear acts on a diff read earlier, with no lock held between. (1) A backfill can finish and stamp between sync's read and sync's clear, so sync writes 0 over a true stamp. If sync then yields, the branch stays unstamped until the next sync's no-work path re-stamps it. (2) A sync that finds work on a `-1` branch with no link change now commits 0 over the sentinel, where main's clear rolled back with a failed embed. The branch becomes backfill-eligible again and is retried and re-marked nightly.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a sync finding work can un-stamp a just-finished branch or clear a content-error sentinel, and the next sync or backfill puts it right.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a sync finding work can un-stamp a just-finished branch or clear a content-error sentinel, and the next sync or backfill puts it right.

findings.title: No test covers the `is_active` filter that moved into sync's lookup
findings.why_it_matters: `test_zero_exchange_inactive_branch_not_stamped` was deleted when the guard moved out of `embed_branch_chunks` into the caller's SQL, and no test covers the clause now. CLAUDE.md says every read path keeps that filter. The critic's other test comparisons were adequate replacements or accepted by the ledger.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: sync's `is_active` filter has no direct test.
findings.chosen: A: Add a test that an inactive branch is not embedded by `embed_session_branch`.
